chapter: Joining Goodman and views on arranging
title: Jingles and Broadway orchestrating
summary: He fails to get jingles, hates orchestrating Broadway, and thinks Sondheim writes thorough scores.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I tried for years to get jingles, because really, that's the only thing there is in New York, and I can't. I can't get near that. I've been dabbling on the west coast because I know one guy out there, but that never matured into anything either. I orchestrate Broadway shows, which is a huge drag, I hate it. I hate it with a
Did you hear what John Tunig did with Sweeney Todd, the orchestrating?
I heard it a few months ago.
That I thought was incredible, the orchestration he did. I think he was given free range and just used his imagination, which is generally the case.
I don't want to say because I don't know, but I think that that guy--what's his name--Sondheim--writes all the stuff out.

Yes, I think he makes a very thorough piano-type score, because I've encountered so much of it, and there's very little you can change in that. That's one of the reasons I hate it, because they rehearse the stuff, especially if you've got a composer, he doesn't want anything
